title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Wachau and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: A Wachau label shows producer, grape, the Vinea Wachau category, like Federspiel, and since 2020 the DAC level: Wachau DAC, village name, or Ried plus vineyard name. Famous producers include F.X. Pichler, Prager, Hirtzberger, Knoll and the Domäne Wachau co-operative.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Steinfeder and Federspiel suit light dishes: salads, river fish, asparagus, Wiener Schnitzel. Smaragd suits richer food: roast pork, chicken in cream, Asian dishes with spice and fish with butter sauce. Wachau apricots, Marillen, are famous; apricot dumplings suit off-dry wines. Serve at 9 to 12 degrees, Smaragd a little warmer.
steps.highlight: Schnitzel with Federspiel, pork with Smaragd

steps.explanation: Wachau apricots are a protected local speciality.

steps.body: A Smaragd Grüner Veltliner with Wiener Schnitzel is a classic Austrian match. The wine's pepper and body handle the fried crust.

steps.prompt: All Wachau Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd wines are dry.
steps.explanation: Yes. The categories are for dry wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show category, DAC and Ried
Federspiel suits schnitzel; Smaragd suits richer dishes
